definition: Automatik Text Reader was a free and open source add-on for Firefox providing text-to-speech functions available from the Mozilla Add-ons collection.
details: It supports multiple languages and accents and is capable of autonomously recognizing the language of written text and activating the respective speech synthesis engine. Amongst the peculiar features, the voice speed is adjustable and the text selection is automatic. In addition to the unique features users will find that the interface is very simple to use; having only 4 buttons to operate it.

explainer.lead: Automatik Text Reader was a free, open-source Firefox add-on that read written text aloud. It detected a passage's language, chose a matching speech-synthesis engine, and kept operation simple with automatic text selection, adjustable speed, and four buttons.

tiers.eli5: It was a small browser add-on that read text on screen out loud for you, figured out what language the text was in, and switched to a voice for that language.
tiers.practitioner: It autonomously recognised the language of written text and activated the respective speech synthesis engine, with adjustable voice speed, automatic text selection, and a simple interface of only 4 buttons. Note it was an add-on for Firefox, not a standalone system.
tiers.paperLevel: Described as a free and open source Firefox add-on from the Mozilla Add-ons collection offering text-to-speech, supporting multiple languages and accents with autonomous language recognition to select the speech synthesis engine; features include adjustable voice speed, automatic text selection, and four interface buttons. No performance figures or supported-language list are given.

explainer.example: A user opens a page in Firefox and lets Automatik Text Reader select a passage in a supported language. The add-on detects the language, activates the corresponding speech engine, and reads the passage aloud; the user can then slow down or speed up the voice.

usedIn.name: Firefox
usedIn.detail: Hosted the add-on, which provided text-to-speech functions for written text in the browser.

usedIn.name: Multilingual speech synthesis
usedIn.detail: Used automatic language recognition to activate the speech-synthesis engine matching each passage.

explainer.intuition: The add-on acts like a multilingual reader inside Firefox: it identifies what language a passage uses before choosing how to speak it. This removes the need for the user to select the language and synthesis engine manually.
howItWorks: The user works with written text in Firefox.
The add-on selects the text automatically.
It recognizes the language of the selected passage.
It activates the speech-synthesis engine for that language.
The engine reads the text aloud, with voice speed adjustable through the simple four-button interface.
explainer.whyItMatters: It combined language detection, engine selection, and playback inside the browser, reducing manual setup for reading multilingual text aloud. Automatic selection and a four-button interface made those functions straightforward to operate.
misconceptions: It was not a translation tool: language recognition was used to choose a speech engine, not to change the text's language.
It was a Firefox add-on that activated speech-synthesis engines, not a standalone synthesis engine itself.
